_readme: Idioms a C64 game developer cannot express, or can express only in a form no competent developer would accept. Each entry is EXECUTABLE: the gate compiles `source` and asserts `expect` still describes what happens. When a gap is fixed the gate goes RED, which is the point — an entry cannot rot silently, it must be retired deliberately. Add an entry when a restriction is discovered; delete it in the same change that removes the restriction.

entries.idiom: Write to screen RAM in a loop — clear the screen, blit text, draw a tile row
entries.governedBy: AR-101 (runtime half) — rationale EXPIRED when slice 7b shipped (zp),Y
entries.note: The frozen spec mandates this form at spec/12-intrinsics.md:159.

entries.idiom: Name a hardware register instead of a magic number
entries.governedBy: none — drift. No decision authorised rejecting a named constant
entries.note: Violates Prime Directive clause 3. The diagnostic text claims to require a compile-time constant and then rejects one.

entries.idiom: Use a constant expression as an address
Call code at an address — a tracker-authored SID player, or a KERNAL routine
entries.note: spec/evaluations/F015-data-inclusion.md:583 builds its embedded-SID example on callAddress(), a helper the language cannot express. Music is unreachable by construction.

entries.idiom: Copy a whole struct out of an array of sprite records
entries.governedBy: slice-7b ST-40 (partial); the spill ceiling is unrecorded
entries.note: spec/07-structs.md:588 uses this exact shape as its own example. Fails as an internal compiler error naming IR nodes, not as a user diagnostic.
A screen-sized 25x40 map. A small map with byte indices folds and compiles; the failure needs a realistic size, which is exactly the shape a game uses.

entries.governedBy: slice-4a AR-3 — deferred to 'alongside Slice 7'; Slice 7 shipped without it
entries.note: `until` is normative spec surface (spec/05, spec/08). Every spec example using it is a syntax error.

entries.idiom: Cast, using the syntax the specification documents
entries.governedBy: none — no ruling found on the syntax divergence
entries.note: spec/02-type-system.md:302 documents byte(expr); grammar.ebnf.md:305 documents `expr as type`; the parser accepts only <byte>(expr). Three different answers.

entries.idiom: Divide by a power of two
entries.note: spec/04-expressions-operators.md:70 and F017:251 promise LSR (2 cycles). Emits a runtime division call instead — roughly 75x. F017 passed its Language Guard on this cost model.

entries.idiom: Use a named constant as the loop step
entries.governedBy: RD-01 Won't-Have — non-literal step deferred to RD-04
entries.note: STRIDE is a positive compile-time constant, but the for-loop step check folds with a resolver-less evalConst, so a named-constant step is rejected as 'must be a positive compile-time constant'. Prime Directive clause 3: an illogical restriction the target user would reasonably write. RD-04 (non-literal step folding) lifts it — the folded value must also reach codegen, since constStep is literal-only today.
